readings.text: The glosses, the 彖, every commentator, Wilhelm and Legge: the brightness wounded, the sun in the earth. The 左傳 reads sun and bird together; 李鏡池 a calling bird, Shaughnessy "Calling Pheasant". Flight, wings, thigh, hunt and heart fit a creature; "Jizi's" fits a condition. We print "the brightness wounded".

readings.title: Not about illness, or not in haste?
readings.text: 王弼, 孔穎達, 程頤, 朱熹, Wilhelm and Legge read 不可疾貞 as "do not hasten to set right". We print the book's frame, what a divination is about before 貞, with 16 貞疾 for illness.

readings.title: Whose strength?
readings.text: In the second line the base's mark and 王弼 cut 用拯馬，壯吉; the same words in 59 and 程頤 make the horse strong. We print the second.

readings.title: Who climbs and falls?
readings.text: The dark lord, the last king of Shang (朱熹, Legge), or the sun (侯果, 虞翻). We print "it".

pinyinTones.name: Míng Yí
pinyinTones.judgment: lì jiān zhēn.
pinyinTones.image: míng rù dì zhōng, míng yí. jūn zǐ yǐ lì zhòng, yòng huì ér míng.
lines: míng yí yú fēi, chuí qí yì. jūn zǐ yú xíng, sān rì bù shí. yǒu yōu wǎng, zhǔ rén yǒu yán.
míng yí, yí yú zuǒ gǔ, yòng zhěng mǎ zhuàng, jí.
míng yí yú nán shòu, dé qí dà shǒu, bù kě jí zhēn.
rù yú zuǒ fù, huò míng yí zhī xīn, yú chū mén tíng.
jī zǐ zhī míng yí, lì zhēn.
bù míng, huì. chū dēng yú tiān, hòu rù yú dì.

pinyinNotes: 夷: yí (wounded), as 陸德明 夷傷也
莅: lì, as 陸德明 履二反
拯: zhěng (to lift, rescue), as 陸德明 拯救之拯

hexagrams.image: 風自火出，家人。君子以言有物而行有恆。

lines.label: 初九
lines.text: 閑有家，悔亡。

lines.label: 六二
lines.text: 无攸遂，在中饋，貞吉。

lines.label: 九三
lines.text: 家人嗃嗃，悔厲，吉；婦子嘻嘻，終吝。

lines.label: 六四
lines.text: 富家，大吉。

lines.label: 九五
lines.text: 王假有家，勿恤，吉。

lines.label: 上九
lines.text: 有孚威如，終吉。

hexagrams.heading: 家人
hexagrams.name: 家人

wilhelm.name: Die Sippe
wilhelm.judgment: Die Sippe. Fördernd ist die Beharrlichkeit der Frau.
wilhelm.image: Der Wind kommt aus dem Feuer hervor: das Bild der Sippe. So hat der Edle in seinen Worten die Sache und in seinem Wandel die Dauer.
lines: Anfangs eine Neun bedeutet: Fester Abschluss innerhalb der Sippe. Reue schwindet.
Sechs auf zweitem Platz bedeutet: Sie soll nicht ihrer Laune folgen. Sie soll im Innern für Speise sorgen. Beharrlichkeit bringt Heil.
Neun auf drittem Platz bedeutet: Wenn es in der Sippe hitzig zugeht, so entsteht Reue über zu große Strenge. Doch Heil! Wenn Weib und Kind tändeln und lachen, so führt das schließlich zu Beschämung.
Sechs auf viertem Platz bedeutet: Sie ist der Reichtum des Hauses. Großes Heil!
Neun auf fünftem Platz bedeutet: Ein König naht er seiner Sippe, fürchtet euch nicht. Heil!
Oben eine Neun bedeutet: Seine Arbeit ist ehrfurchtgebietend. Schließlich kommt Heil.
wilhelm.source: Richard Wilhelm, I Ging (Jena, 1924), as transcribed with modernised spelling at schuledesrades.org

legge.name: Kiâ Zăn
legge.judgment: For (the realisation of what is taught in) Kiâ Zăn, (or for the regulation of the family), what is most advantageous is that the wife be firm and correct.
legge.image: (The trigram representing) fire, and that for wind coming forth from it, form Kiâ Zăn. The superior man, in accordance with this, orders his words according to (the truth of) things, and his conduct so that it is uniformly consistent.
lines: The first line, undivided, shows its subject establishing restrictive regulations in his household. Occasion for repentance will disappear.
The second line, divided, shows its subject taking nothing on herself, but in her central place attending to the preparation of the food. Through her firm correctness there will be good fortune.

The third line, undivided, shows its subject (treating) the members of the household with stern severity. There will be occasion for repentance, there will be peril, (but) there will (also) be good fortune. If the wife and children were to be smirking and chattering, in the end there would be occasion for regret.
The fourth line, divided, shows its subject enriching the family. There will be great good fortune.
The fifth line, undivided, shows the influence of the king extending to his family. There need be no anxiety; there will be good fortune.
The topmost line, undivided, shows its subject possessed of sincerity and arrayed in majesty. In the end there will be good fortune.
legge.source: James Legge, The Yi King (Sacred Books of the East 16, 1882), pp. 136-138 (Image: Appendix II, p. 312)

en.name: The Clan
en.nameNote: 家人 is "the people of the house": 家 is a dwelling (說文), the inside of a house (爾雅). The same two words close a wedding song: the girl goes to her husband's house, "宜其家人" (桃夭).
en.judgment: A favourable divination for a woman.
en.judgmentNote: The formula alone: a divination for a woman. Such divinations stand in the rites of marriage, where the turtle is consulted and the reading sent: "占曰吉" (儀禮, 士昏禮). The book has nothing more for the words.
en.tradition: 家人 is the people of one house; the fifth and second lines are each right in their places, outside and inside. "Favourable for a woman's being right": the inside is to be set right first, and when it is right, nothing outside will be wrong.
en.image: Wind comes out from fire: The Clan. So the noble one's words have substance and his conduct has constancy.
en.imageNote: A later layer, and moral in its own words. 有物 is a phrase of the songs: "有物有則", where there are things there are rules (烝民). Fire takes wood for its house and blazes with wind, as husband and wife need each other (馬融).

lines.text: Drilling the house. Regret gone.
lines.note: 有 before a name is the Zhou particle, as in "有周" (文王): so 有家 is "the house". 閑 is to drill, as 26 九三 (鄭玄 "習也"). 王弼 and 程頤 read it as guarding: where people live together there is always regret, done away with by guarding.

lines.text: Nothing to go on to: within, the presenting of food. The divination: auspicious.
lines.note: 饋 is presenting food at the offering, the name of two rites in the 儀禮, where the wife of the house has her own part in the side room. A song gives a daughter "wine and food" as her concern (斯干). Who is within the line does not say.

lines.text: The household: harsh, harsh. Regret, danger; auspicious. Wife and children: laughing, laughing. In the end, trouble.
lines.note: 嘻 in the songs is a cry (噫嘻). 婦子, wife and children, take food to the fields in 七月. 嗃嗃 is read as harsh (侯果); 馬融 reads contentment, 鄭玄 suffering heat, and 程頤 says the sense is not certain to him.

lines.text: Enriching the house: very auspicious.
lines.note: 大吉 is a Shang verdict (合集 28563.1). In a Warring States Chu almanac a very auspicious day is good for taking a wife, offering, and building a house (九店 13下). 富 is the verb, as in 9 九五.

lines.text: The king comes to the house. Do not be anxious: auspicious.
lines.note: 假 is 格, to come: at dawn the king came into the great hall (晉侯穌編鐘); in the songs spirits brightly come down (烝民). The same words with the temple for the house open 45 and 59. 朱熹: an auspicious reading for taking a royal consort.

lines.text: There is confirmation, awesome. In the end, auspicious.
lines.note: 威, awe, is the bronzes' 威儀. 有孚 and 威如 stand together in 14 六五. What is founded on love lacks awe, so the way of the house values awe (王弼).

essays.title: Fire within, wind without
essays.text: The lower trigram is fire, the upper wind: "wind comes out from fire". The 彖 reads the second and fifth lines as wife and husband in their places, the woman within and the man without, and the house as the root of the realm: set the house right and the world is settled. The 序卦: one wounded outside must come back home.

readings.title: Drilling or guarding?
readings.text: 鄭玄 reads 閑 as "習也", as in 26 九三, where the book fixed "to drill". 馬融 reads a barrier, followed here by 王弼, 程頤, 朱熹, Wilhelm and Legge. We print "drilling", the standing rendering.

readings.title: Harsh, content, or burning?
readings.text: Harsh: 侯果, 王弼, 孔穎達, 朱熹, Wilhelm, Legge. Content and at ease: 馬融. Suffering heat: 鄭玄. 程頤 says the sense is uncertain. We print "harsh, harsh".

readings.title: Enriching the house, or its wealth?
readings.text: 王弼, 程頤, 朱熹 and Legge make 富 a verb, enriching the house; Wilhelm has "she is the wealth of the house". We print the verb.

readings.title: Whose part is the food?
readings.text: The commentators and both translators give the second line to the wife; the Chinese names no one. We print it without a subject.

pinyinTones.name: Jiā Rén
pinyinTones.judgment: lì nǚ zhēn.
pinyinTones.image: fēng zì huǒ chū, jiā rén. jūn zǐ yǐ yán yǒu wù ér xíng yǒu héng.
lines: xián yǒu jiā, huǐ wáng.
wú yōu suì, zài zhōng kuì, zhēn jí.
jiā rén hè hè, huǐ lì, jí; fù zǐ xī xī, zhōng lìn.
fù jiā, dà jí.
wáng gé yǒu jiā, wù xù, jí.
yǒu fú wēi rú, zhōng jí.

pinyinNotes: 嗃: hè, as 陸德明 呼落反
嘻: xī, as 陸德明 喜悲反
假: gé (to come to, 至也), as 陸德明 更白反, not jiǎ

hexagrams.image: 上火下澤，睽。君子以同而異。

lines.label: 初九
lines.text: 悔亡。喪馬，勿逐，自復。見惡人，无咎。

lines.label: 九二
lines.text: 遇主于巷，无咎。

lines.label: 六三
lines.text: 見輿曳，其牛掣，其人天且劓，无初有終。

lines.label: 九四
lines.text: 睽孤，遇元夫，交孚，厲，无咎。

lines.label: 六五
lines.text: 悔亡。厥宗噬膚，往何咎？

lines.label: 上九
lines.text: 睽孤，見豕負塗，載鬼一車，先張之弧，後說之弧，匪寇，婚媾。往遇雨，則吉。

hexagrams.heading: 睽
hexagrams.name: 睽

wilhelm.name: Der Gegensatz
wilhelm.judgment: Der Gegensatz. In kleinen Sachen Heil.
wilhelm.image: Oben das Feuer, unten der See: das Bild des Gegensatzes. So behält der Edle bei aller Gemeinschaft seine Besonderheit.
lines: Anfangs eine Neun bedeutet: Die Reue schwindet. Wenn du dein Pferd verlierst, so lauf ihm nicht nach. Es kommt von selber wieder. Wenn du böse Menschen siehst, so hüte dich vor Fehlern.
Neun auf zweitem Platz bedeutet: Man begegnet seinem Herrn in enger Gasse. Kein Makel.
Sechs auf drittem Platz bedeutet: Man sieht den Wagen nach hinten gezerrt, die Rinder festgehalten, dem Menschen Haare und Nase abgeschnitten. Kein guter Anfang, aber ein gutes Ende.
Neun auf viertem Platz bedeutet: Durch Gegensatz vereinsamt, trifft man einen Gleichgesinnten, mit dem man in Treue verkehren kann. Trotz der Gefahr kein Makel.
Sechs auf fünftem Platz bedeutet: Die Reue schwindet. Der Gefährte beißt sich durch die Hülle. Wenn man hingeht zu ihm, wie wäre das ein Fehler?

Oben eine Neun bedeutet: Durch Gegensatz vereinsamt, sieht man seinen Gefährten wie ein schmutzbeladenes Schwein, wie einen Wagen voll Teufel. Erst spannt man den Bogen nach ihm, dann legt man den Bogen weg. Nicht Räuber er ist, will freien zur Frist. Beim Hingehen fällt Regen, dann kommt Heil.
wilhelm.source: Richard Wilhelm, I Ging (Jena, 1924), as transcribed with modernised spelling at schuledesrades.org

legge.name: Khwei
legge.judgment: Khwei indicates that, (notwithstanding the condition of things which it denotes), in small matters there will (still) be good success.
legge.image: (The trigram representing) fire above, and that for (the waters of) a marsh below, form Khwei. The superior man, in accordance with this, where there is a general agreement, yet admits diversity.
lines: The first line, undivided, shows that (to its subject) occasion for repentance will disappear. He has lost his horses, but let him not seek for them;—they will return of themselves. Should he meet with bad men, he will not err (in communicating with them).
The second line, undivided, shows its subject happening to meet with his lord in a bye-passage. There will be no error.

In the third line, divided, we see one whose carriage is dragged back, while the oxen in it are pushed back, and he is himself subjected to the shaving of his head and the cutting off of his nose. There is no good beginning, but there will be a good end.

The fourth line, undivided, shows its subject solitary amidst the (prevailing) disunion. (But) he meets with the good man (represented by the first line), and they blend their sincere desires together. The position is one of peril, but there will be no mistake.

The fifth line, divided, shows that (to its subject) occasion for repentance will disappear. With his relative (and minister he unites closely and readily) as if he were biting through a piece of skin. When he goes forward (with this help), what error can there be?

The topmost line, undivided, shows its subject solitary amidst the (prevailing) disunion. (In the subject of the third line, he seems to) see a pig bearing on its back a load of mud, (or fancies) there is a carriage full of ghosts. He first bends his bow against him, and afterwards unbends it, (for he discovers) that he is not an assailant to injure, but a near relative. Going forward, he shall meet with (genial) rain, and there will be good fortune.
legge.source: James Legge, The Yi King (Sacred Books of the East 16, 1882), pp. 139-140 (Image: Appendix II, p. 314)

en.name: Opposition
en.nameNote: 睽 is a matter of the eyes: "目不相視也", eyes that do not look at each other (說文). The 序卦: "乖也", at odds; the 雜卦: turned outward. In the lines it stands in 睽孤, "estranged, alone".
en.judgment: In small matters: auspicious.
en.judgmentNote: The Chu slip has the judgment word for word. Shang and Chu divinations sort matters by size, as 3's 小貞吉，大貞凶. The book has nothing more for 小事.
en.tradition: 睽 is being at odds: fire above and the lake below go against each other's nature; the middle and the youngest daughter will not marry into the same house. The reading: not for great matters, but in small ones there is still a way to good fortune.
en.image: Fire above, the lake below: Opposition. So the noble one is at one with others and yet apart.
en.imageNote: A later layer, and moral in its own words. One with others in the common order of things, apart in one's own office (王弼). The hundred officers differ in their duties and all come back to good order (荀爽).

lines.text: Regret gone. Losing horses: do not chase them; they come back of themselves. Seeing bad men: no blame.
lines.note: An early order of the lord of Lu: if horses and oxen run loose and bondmen run away, do not dare to chase them; return them duly (尚書, 費誓). 勿, 逐 and 復, the words of this line, in one order. 朱熹: he must see bad men, as Confucius saw Yang Huo.

lines.text: Meeting the host in the lane. No blame.
lines.note: 巷 is the lane within a ward (說文); in a song the lanes are empty when Shu goes hunting (叔于田). 主, the host, as 2 and 36. The Chu slip has the line word for word. 王弼: the two meet without arranging it.

lines.text: Seeing the cart dragged, its ox held back; its man branded on the forehead, and his nose cut off. No beginning, but an end reached.
lines.note: Branding and cutting off the nose are punishments of Zhou law (康誥; 周禮, 司刑). 天 is "剠也", the forehead cut and inked (馬融). The 說文 quotes the line for an ox with one horn raised. The Chu slip has the cart stopped.

lines.text: Estranged, alone: meeting the first man. Crossing trust. Danger; no blame.
lines.note: In 645 BC a scribe read a marriage oracle as "歸妹睽孤，寇張之弧", estranged, alone: raiders draw their bows (左傳): words of this line and the top one. 元 is first, as 元子, the eldest son. 夫 is a grown man, not a husband (孔穎達).

lines.text: Regret gone. At its ancestral temple, biting the skin-meat: going on, what blame?
lines.note: The Chu slip has 陞宗噬膚, going up to the ancestral temple: 宗 is a place, as in 13. 膚 is the skin-meat of the offering cauldron (少牢饋食禮), eaten by the kin. The commentators read 宗 as its kin, the second line.

lines.text: Estranged, alone: seeing a pig carrying mud on its back, one cart loaded with ghosts. First drawing the bow, afterwards loosening the bow. Not raiders: a marriage. Going on, meeting rain: then auspicious.
lines.note: The 左傳 verse of 645 BC puts 睽孤, raiders and the drawn bow in one oracle about a marriage. A peach-wood bow drove off calamity (左傳, 538 BC). 鬼 may be ghosts or the Gui people (鬼方). The Shang divined about rain and recorded it.

essays.title: Fire above the lake
essays.text: The lower trigram is the lake, the upper fire. The 彖: fire moves up, the lake moves down; two women live together, and their minds do not go the same way, fire being the middle daughter and the lake the youngest. The lines speak of losing and meeting: horses lost and come back, the host met in a lane, a first man met, an ancestral temple, a cart of ghosts that turns out to be a wedding.

readings.title: Held back, or horns askew?
readings.text: 王弼, 孔穎達, 程頤, Wilhelm and Legge read 掣 as held back. The oldest glosses read the ox's horns: both raised (鄭玄), one raised (子夏傳; the 說文), one down one up (荀爽, 虞翻), but on another graph. We print the base's 掣 with its own sense.

readings.title: Its ancestral temple, or its kin?
readings.text: 王弼, 孔穎達, 程頤, 朱熹, Wilhelm and Legge read 厥宗 as its kin, the second line. The book's 宗 in 13 and the Chu 陞宗 make it the temple. We print the temple.

readings.title: The bow, or the jar?
readings.text: 京房, 馬融, 鄭玄, 王肅 and 李鼎祚's text write the second 弧 as 壺: "afterwards setting down the jar", hostility turning to a wedding feast. We print the base: "loosening the bow".

readings.title: Branded, or shaven?
readings.text: 天 is the forehead branded (馬融, 虞翻, 孔穎達) or the head shaved (程頤, 朱熹, Wilhelm, Legge). We print "branded on the forehead".

readings.title: Ghosts, or Gui men?
readings.text: Every commentator reads ghosts. The Gui of 鬼方 would make the cart a cart of strangers. We print "ghosts".

pinyinTones.name: Kuí
pinyinTones.judgment: xiǎo shì jí.
pinyinTones.image: shàng huǒ xià zé, kuí. jūn zǐ yǐ tóng ér yì.
lines: huǐ wáng. sàng mǎ, wù zhú, zì fù. jiàn è rén, wú jiù.
yù zhǔ yú xiàng, wú jiù.
jiàn yú yè, qí niú chè, qí rén tiān qiě yì, wú chū yǒu zhōng.
kuí gū, yù yuán fū, jiāo fú, lì, wú jiù.
huǐ wáng. jué zōng shì fū, wǎng hé jiù?
kuí gū, jiàn shǐ fù tú, zài guǐ yī chē, xiān zhāng zhī hú, hòu tuō zhī hú, fěi kòu, hūn gòu. wǎng yù yǔ, zé jí.

pinyinNotes: 睽: kuí, as 陸德明 苦圭反
復: fù (to return), as 陸德明 音服
見: jiàn (to meet, to see) throughout
掣: chè, as 陸德明 昌逝反
劓: yì, as 陸德明 魚器反
說: tuō (to unstring, read 脫), as 陸德明 吐活反
弧: hú, as 陸德明 音胡
匪: fěi (not, 非)

hexagrams.judgment: 利西南，不利東北。利見大人。貞吉。
hexagrams.image: 山上有水，蹇。君子以反身修德。

lines.label: 初六
lines.text: 往蹇來譽。

lines.label: 六二
lines.text: 王臣蹇蹇，匪躬之故。

lines.label: 九三
lines.text: 往蹇來反。

lines.label: 六四
lines.text: 往蹇來連。

lines.label: 九五
lines.text: 大蹇，朋來。

lines.label: 上六
lines.text: 往蹇，來碩，吉，利見大人。

hexagrams.heading: 蹇
hexagrams.name: 蹇

wilhelm.name: Das Hemmnis
wilhelm.judgment: Das Hemmnis. Fördernd ist der Südwesten. Nicht fördernd ist der Nordosten. Fördernd ist es, den großen Mann zu sehen. Beharrlichkeit ist von Heil.
wilhelm.image: Auf dem Berg ist das Wasser: das Bild des Hemmnisses. So wendet sich der Edle seiner eigenen Person zu und bildet seinen Charakter.
lines: Anfangs eine Sechs bedeutet: Gehen führt in Hemmnisse, Kommen findet Lob.
Sechs auf zweitem Platz bedeutet: Des Königs Diener ist in Hemmnis über Hemmnis. Aber es ist nicht seine eigene Schuld.
Neun auf drittem Platz bedeutet: Gehen führt in Hemmnisse; da kommt er zurück.
Sechs auf viertem Platz bedeutet: Gehen führt in Hemmnisse, Kommen führt zur Vereinigung.
Neun auf fünftem Platz bedeutet: Inmitten der größten Hemmnisse kommen Freunde.
Oben eine Sechs bedeutet: Gehen führt in Hemmnisse, Kommen führt zu großem Heil. Fördernd ist es, den großen Mann zu sehen.
wilhelm.source: Richard Wilhelm, I Ging (Jena, 1924), as transcribed with modernised spelling at schuledesrades.org

legge.name: Kien
legge.judgment: In (the state indicated by) Kien advantage will be found in the south-west, and the contrary in the north-east. It will be advantageous (also) to meet with the great man. (In these circumstances), with firmness and correctness, there will be good fortune.
legge.image: (The trigram representing) a mountain, and above it that for water, form Kien. The superior man, in accordance with this, turns round (and examines) himself, and cultivates his virtue.
lines: From the first line, divided, we learn that advance (on the part of its subject) will lead to (greater) difficulties, while remaining stationary will afford ground for praise.
The second line, divided, shows the minister of the king struggling with difficulty on difficulty, and not with a view to his own advantage.
The third line, undivided, shows its subject advancing, (but only) to (greater) difficulties. He remains stationary, and returns (to his former associates).
The fourth line, divided, shows its subject advancing, (but only) to (greater) difficulties. He remains stationary, and unites (with the subject of the line above).
The fifth line, undivided, shows its subject struggling with the greatest difficulties, while friends are coming to help him.

The topmost line, divided, shows its subject going forward, (only to increase) the difficulties, while his remaining stationary will be (productive of) great (merit). There will be good fortune, and it will be advantageous to meet with the great man.
legge.source: James Legge, The Yi King (Sacred Books of the East 16, 1882), pp. 141-143 (Image: Appendix II, p. 315)

en.name: Hindrance
en.nameNote: 蹇 is lameness: in Qin and Jin speech the lame, whose body is long on one side and short on the other (方言); "the lame walk hobbling" (郭璞). 朱熹: the feet cannot go forward. The wings take the hardness for the sense: "難也".
en.judgment: Favourable to the southwest; not favourable to the northeast. Favourable to see the great man. The divination: auspicious.
en.judgmentNote: 2's judgment has the same two directions. Qin almanacs, later than the text, give directions their verdicts by the day: "on shen days, southwest auspicious, north disaster" (睡虎地 日書甲 136正參). The great man in the songs reads dreams. The Chu slip lacks 貞吉.
en.tradition: The mountain below the water: seeing the peril and stopping. The southwest is level and easy, the northeast steep; in hardship one should not run into peril. One must see the great man to get across, and hold to what is right to be auspicious; who sees peril may stop, but not for good.
en.image: On the mountain there is water: Hindrance. So the noble one turns back to himself and cultivates his virtue.
en.imageNote: A later layer, and moral in its own words. In 686 BC a Lu duke refused to attack: "it is I who lack virtue ... let us attend to our virtue and wait for the time" (左傳). Water belongs below the mountain and must turn back down (陸績).

lines.text: Going on: limping. Coming: praise.
lines.note: The Chu slip has the line word for word. 譽, praise, is the good name a lord keeps in the songs: "以永終譽" (振鷺). The small image: "it is fitting to wait". 程頤: to go up is 往, not to go is 來.

lines.text: The king's servant: limping, limping. Not on account of his own person.
lines.note: 王臣 in the bronzes is a class of the king's servants, given in gifts (大盂鼎). The songs: "to the shores of the land there is no man not the king's servant; I alone toil" (北山). In a Lu levy even the limping marched (國語). No verdict, which 朱熹 remarks on.

lines.text: Going on: limping. Coming: turning back.
lines.note: The Chu slip has the line without 蹇. 反 is turning back, as 9 九三 反目. 程頤: going home, as the annals say "returned". The small image: those within are glad of it.

lines.text: Going on: limping. Coming: joined.
lines.note: The Chu slip has the line word for word. 連 is joined: to the fifth (荀爽), to those below (程頤), to the third (朱熹). 馬融 reads "also hardship", 鄭玄 "slow", 虞翻 the hand-cart 輦 the levy hauls in the songs (黍苗).

lines.text: Greatly limping: friends come.
lines.note: 朋來 "friends come" is 24's judgment. 干寶: this stands for King Wen imprisoned, and the friends for the ministers who saved him. 程頤: no verdict, because the friends are not enough to get it across.

lines.text: Going on: limping. Coming: big. Auspicious. Favourable to see the great man.
lines.note: 碩, big, in the songs is said of people and creatures: "碩人其頎" (碩人), and the big rat (碩鼠). 說文: "頭大也". The Chu slip has the line word for word. Only this line has 吉 (程頤).

essays.title: Water on the mountain
essays.text: The lower trigram is the mountain, keeping still; the upper water, the pit. The 彖: the peril is in front; to see the peril and be able to stop is wise. 蹇 stands in every line, and four of the six have the frame "going on: limping; coming: ...". The 序卦 puts it after 睽 and before 解, whose judgment opens with this one's "favourable to the southwest".

readings.title: Limping, or hardship?
readings.text: Lameness is the word's sense in the 方言, in 韋昭, and in 朱熹's gloss; the wings and 陸德明 give hardship, and every commentator reads the lines so, with Wilhelm and Legge. Shaughnessy names the hexagram "Lame". We print "limping" in the lines and Wilhelm's "Hindrance" for the name.

readings.title: Coming, or staying?
readings.text: 程頤: not going is 來; Legge: "remaining stationary". 王弼 and 朱熹 give a coming back or down. We print "coming", which leaves the direction to the reader as the Chinese does.

readings.title: For his own sake, or his own doing?
readings.text: Every commentator and Legge: not for his own sake. Wilhelm: not his own fault. The Chu slip has 今 for 躬. We print "not on account of his own person", which holds both.

readings.title: Which southwest?
readings.text: The commentators place the trigrams on the compass (虞翻, 程頤, 朱熹). Legge inclines to the Zhou lands of the south and west against the Shang in the north and east, which the sources do not test. We translate the words and add nothing.

pinyinTones.name: Jiǎn
pinyinTones.judgment: lì xī nán, bù lì dōng běi. lì jiàn dà rén. zhēn jí.
pinyinTones.image: shān shàng yǒu shuǐ, jiǎn. jūn zǐ yǐ fǎn shēn xiū dé.
lines: wǎng jiǎn lái yù.
wáng chén jiǎn jiǎn, fěi gōng zhī gù.
wǎng jiǎn lái fǎn.
wǎng jiǎn lái lián.
dà jiǎn, péng lái.
wǎng jiǎn, lái shuò, jí, lì jiàn dà rén.

pinyinNotes: 蹇: jiǎn, as 陸德明 紀免反
連: lián (joined), the plain sense the book takes with 鄭玄's 如字, against 陸德明's 力善反 (liǎn)
匪: fěi (not, 非)
碩: shuò (great)

hexagrams.judgment: 利西南。无所往，其來復吉。有攸往，夙吉。
hexagrams.image: 雷雨作，解。君子以赦過宥罪。

lines.label: 初六
lines.text: 无咎。

lines.label: 九二
lines.text: 田獲三狐，得黃矢，貞吉。

lines.label: 六三
lines.text: 負且乘，致寇至，貞吝。

lines.label: 九四
lines.text: 解而拇，朋至斯孚。

lines.label: 六五
lines.text: 君子維有解，吉，有孚于小人。

lines.label: 上六
lines.text: 公用射隼于高墉之上，獲之，无不利。

hexagrams.heading: 解
hexagrams.name: 解

wilhelm.name: Die Befreiung
wilhelm.judgment: Die Befreiung. Fördernd ist der Südwesten. Wenn nichts mehr da ist, wohin man zu gehen hätte, ist das Wiederkommen von Heil. Wenn es noch etwas gibt, wohin man gehen muss, dann ist Raschheit von Heil.
wilhelm.image: Donner und Regen erheben sich: das Bild der Befreiung. So verzeiht der Edle Fehler und vergibt die Schuld.
lines: Anfangs eine Sechs bedeutet: Ohne Makel.
Neun auf zweitem Platz bedeutet: Auf dem Feld erlegt man drei Füchse und bekommt einen gelben Pfeil. Beharrlichkeit ist von Heil.
Sechs auf drittem Platz bedeutet: Wenn einer eine Last auf dem Rücken trägt und trotzdem auf dem Wagen fährt, veranlasst er dadurch die Räuber, herbeizukommen. Beharrlichkeit führt zu Beschämung.
Neun auf viertem Platz bedeutet: Befreie dich von deiner großen Zehe. Dann kommt der Gefährte herbei, und dem kannst du trauen.
Sechs auf fünftem Platz bedeutet: Wenn der Edle sich nur befreien kann, das bringt Heil. Er zeigt so den Gemeinen, dass es ihm ernst ist.
Oben eine Sechs bedeutet: Der Fürst schießt nach einem Habicht auf hoher Mauer. Er erlegt ihn. Alles ist fördernd.
wilhelm.source: Richard Wilhelm, I Ging (Jena, 1924), as transcribed with modernised spelling at schuledesrades.org

legge.name: Kieh
legge.judgment: In (the state indicated by) Kieh advantage will be found in the south-west. If no (further) operations be called for, there will be good fortune in coming back (to the old conditions). If some operations be called for, there will be good fortune in the early conducting of them.
legge.image: (The trigram representing) thunder and that for rain, with these phenomena in a state of manifestation, form Kieh. The superior man, in accordance with this, forgives errors, and deals gently with crimes.
lines: The first line, divided, shows that its subject will commit no error.
The second line, undivided, shows its subject catch, in hunting, three foxes, and obtain the yellow (=golden) arrows. With firm correctness there will be good fortune.

The third line, divided, shows a porter with his burden, (yet) riding in a carriage. He will (only) tempt robbers to attack him. However firm and correct he may (try to) be, there will be cause for regret.
(To the subject of) the fourth line, undivided, (it is said), ‘Remove your toes. Friends will (then) come, between you and whom there will be mutual confidence.’

The fifth line, divided, shows (its subject), the superior man (=the ruler), executing his function of removing (whatever is injurious to the idea of the hexagram), in which case there will be good fortune, and confidence in him will be shown even by the small men.
In the sixth line, divided, we see a feudal prince (with his bow) shooting at a falcon on the top of a high wall, and hitting it. (The effect of his action) will be in every way advantageous.
legge.source: James Legge, The Yi King (Sacred Books of the East 16, 1882), pp. 144-145 (Image: Appendix II, p. 316)

en.name: Liberation
en.nameNote: 解 is to untie, to take apart: a knife parting an ox's horn (說文). The 序卦: "緩也", a slackening. In the Chu divination records 解 is a rite, the untying of a curse or harm named in the reading (包山 198, 211).
en.judgment: Favourable to the southwest. Nowhere to go: its coming back, auspicious. Somewhere to go: early, auspicious.
en.judgmentNote: The southwest as in 39, where Qin almanacs give directions their verdicts. 夙, early, is the songs' word for the start of the day's work: "夙興夜寐" (小宛). 來復, coming back, is 24's judgment. The Chu slip has the judgment word for word.
en.tradition: 解 is the scattering of hardship. Once it is untied, the level, easy and quiet is favourable, not long trouble: so the southwest. If there is nowhere to go, come back to one's place and be still; if there is still somewhere to go, go early and come back early.
en.image: Thunder and rain rise: Liberation. So the noble one pardons faults and forgives crimes.
en.imageNote: A later layer, and moral in its own words. Pardon by kind of offence is in the early Zhou documents (梓材, 康誥); the 周禮 counts three leniencies and three pardons, a fault by mistake among them. 程頤: a mistake may be let off; a crime only treated leniently.

lines.text: No blame.
lines.note: The verdict alone, as 32 九二; the Chu slip has it so. 程頤: at the start of untying, rest; the line's few words show it.

lines.text: In the field, catching three foxes, getting a yellow arrow. The divination: auspicious.
lines.note: Foxes were taken in the winter hunt for furs (七月). Zhou kings gave arrows, coloured, as gifts (虢季子白盤), and an arrow found in a falcon in Chen was named by Confucius (國語). 虞翻: the arrow through the fox. 朱熹: an auspicious reading for divining about a hunt.

lines.text: Carrying on the back, and riding: it brings raiders on. The divination: trouble.
lines.note: The 繫辭上, a later wing, reads it: carrying on the back is the small man's work, the carriage the nobleman's; when a small man rides in it, thieves think of taking it. The levy carried loads and pulled carts (黍苗). The Chu slip lacks 貞吝.

lines.text: Untying your big toe. Friends arrive: then, trust.
lines.note: 而 is "you" (孔穎達); the Chu slip has 其, its. 拇 is the big toe, as in 31. The book loosens fetters from the feet in 4 初六. 朋至 stands beside 39 九五 朋來. Whether the toe here is bound the sources do not say.

lines.text: The nobleman: there is untying. Auspicious. There is confirmation in the small men.
lines.note: 程頤: 有孚 is what people now call "seeing it verified"; 朱熹: "孚，驗也", the untying verified by the small men's withdrawing. 君子 and 小人 are the pair of ranks. 維 is the particle (孔穎達 "辭也"); the small image drops it.

lines.text: The duke uses it in shooting a falcon on top of a high wall: catching it. Nothing is unfavourable.
lines.note: A falcon came down dead in the court of Chen with a stone-tipped arrow through it (國語). 墉 is a wall, as 13 九四. The 繫辭下 reads it: the nobleman keeps the tool on his person and waits for the time to move.

essays.title: Thunder over water
essays.text: The lower trigram is water, the pit; the upper thunder, moving. The 彖: heaven and earth come loose, thunder and rain rise, and the fruits, plants and trees all split their sheaths. The figure is 39 turned over, and the judgment opens with 39's "favourable to the southwest" without its northeast. The lines speak of a hunt, a load and a carriage, and untying.

readings.title: Untying, or the state untied?
readings.text: 孔穎達 reads the name xiè, the state after untying, with the wings' "slackening". The lines use 解 as a verb with an object and as a noun. We print "untying" in the lines and Wilhelm's "Liberation" for the name.

readings.title: Your toe, or its toe?
readings.text: 而 is "your" (孔穎達; Wilhelm, Legge); the Chu slip has 其, "its". We print the base, "your".

readings.title: A particle, or bound?
readings.text: 維 in the fifth line is the particle (孔穎達; the small image omits it), or "only" (程頤). Read as the verb of 17 and 29 it would give "bound, there is untying". We print the particle, without a word.

readings.title: A hunt, or a figure?
readings.text: 朱熹: a reading for divining about a hunt. 程頤 and others: the three foxes are three small men. We print the hunt's words and leave the figure to the commentators.

readings.title: Falcon or dove?
readings.text: The commentators and 韋昭: a bird of prey. The 說文: a form of the turtledove. We print "a falcon".

pinyinTones.name: Xiè
pinyinTones.judgment: lì xī nán. wú suǒ wǎng, qí lái fù jí. yǒu yōu wǎng, sù jí.
pinyinTones.image: léi yǔ zuò, xiè. jūn zǐ yǐ shè guò yòu zuì.
lines: wú jiù.
tián huò sān hú, dé huáng shǐ, zhēn jí.
fù qiě chéng, zhì kòu zhì, zhēn lìn.
jiě ér mǔ, péng zhì sī fú.
jūn zǐ wéi yǒu xiè, jí, yǒu fú yú xiǎo rén.
gōng yòng shè sǔn yú gāo yōng zhī shàng, huò zhī, wú bù lì.

pinyinNotes: 解 (the name and 維有解): xiè, as 陸德明 音蟹 (and 孔穎達's 解 as the state of being untied)
解 (解而拇): jiě (to untie), as 陸德明 佳買反
乘: chéng (to ride), as 陸德明 如字
宥: yòu, as 陸德明 音又
射: shè (to shoot), as 陸德明 食亦反

hexagrams.judgment: 有孚，元吉，无咎，可貞。利有攸往。曷之用，二簋可用享。
hexagrams.image: 山下有澤，損。君子以懲忿窒欲。

lines.label: 初九
lines.text: 已事遄往，无咎。酌損之。

lines.label: 九二
lines.text: 利貞。征凶，弗損，益之。

lines.label: 六三
lines.text: 三人行則損一人，一人行則得其友。

lines.label: 六四
lines.text: 損其疾，使遄有喜，无咎。

lines.label: 六五
lines.text: 或益之，十朋之龜弗克違，元吉。

lines.label: 上九
lines.text: 弗損，益之，无咎，貞吉，利有攸往，得臣无家。

hexagrams.heading: 損
hexagrams.name: 損

wilhelm.name: Die Minderung
wilhelm.judgment: Minderung verbunden mit Wahrhaftigkeit wirkt erhabenes Heil ohne Makel. Man kann darin beharrlich sein. Fördernd ist es, etwas zu unternehmen. Wie übt man das aus? Zwei kleine Schüsselchen mag man benützen zum Opfer.
wilhelm.image: Unten am Berg ist der See: das Bild der Minderung. So bändigt der Edle seinen Zorn und hemmt seine Triebe.
lines: Anfangs eine Neun bedeutet: Wenn die Geschäfte fertig sind, rasch hingehen ist kein Makel. Doch muss man überlegen, wie weit man andre mindern darf.
Neun auf zweitem Platz bedeutet: Fördernd ist Beharrlichkeit. Etwas zu unternehmen, ist von Unheil. Ohne sich selbst zu mindern, vermag man die andern zu mehren.
Sechs auf drittem Platz bedeutet: Wenn drei Menschen miteinander wandern, so vermindern sie sich um einen Menschen. Wenn ein Mensch wandert, so findet er seinen Gefährten.
Sechs auf viertem Platz bedeutet: Wenn man seine Mängel mindert macht man, dass der andre eilig kommt und Freude hat. Kein Makel.
Sechs auf fünftem Platz bedeutet: Es mehrt ihn wohl jemand. Zehn Paar Schildkröten können dem nicht widerstreben. Erhabenes Heil!

Oben eine Neun bedeutet: Wenn man ohne Minderung der anderen gemehrt wird, so ist das kein Makel. Beharrlichkeit bringt Heil. Fördernd ist es, etwas zu unternehmen. Man bekommt Diener, aber hat kein besonderes Heim mehr.
wilhelm.source: Richard Wilhelm, I Ging (Jena, 1924), as transcribed with modernised spelling at schuledesrades.org

legge.name: Sun
legge.judgment: In (what is denoted by) Sun, if there be sincerity (in him who employs it), there will be great good fortune:—freedom from error; firmness and correctness that can be maintained; and advantage in every movement that shall be made. In what shall this (sincerity in the exercise of Sun) be employed? (Even) in sacrifice two baskets of grain, (though there be nothing else), may be presented.
legge.image: (The trigram representing) a mountain and beneath it that for the waters of a marsh form Sun. The superior man, in accordance with this, restrains his wrath and represses his desires.
lines: The first line, undivided, shows its subject suspending his own affairs, and hurrying away (to help the subject of the fourth line). He will commit no error, but let him consider how far he should contribute of what is his (for the other).

The second line, undivided, shows that it will be advantageous for its subject to maintain a firm correctness, and that action on his part will be evil. He can give increase (to his correlate) without taking from himself.
The third line, divided, shows how of three men walking together, the number is diminished by one; and how one, walking, finds his friend.
The fourth line, divided, shows its subject diminishing the ailment under which he labours by making (the subject of the first line) hasten (to his help), and make him glad. There will be no error.
The fifth line, divided, shows parties adding to (the stores of) its subject ten pairs of tortoise shells, and accepting no refusal. There will be great good fortune.

The topmost line, undivided, shows its subject giving increase to others without taking from himself. There will be no error. With firm correctness there will be good fortune. There will be advantage in every movement that shall be made. He will find ministers more than can be counted by their clans.
legge.source: James Legge, The Yi King (Sacred Books of the East 16, 1882), pp. 146-148 (Image: Appendix II, p. 317)

en.name: Reduction
en.nameNote: 損 is to reduce, to take away: "虧減之義也", also "to lose" (陸德明). The 彖: reducing what is below and adding to what is above. In the lines 損 is "reducing", and its pair 益 "adding to".
en.judgment: There is confirmation. Greatly auspicious. No blame. It may be divined. Favourable to have somewhere to go. What is to be used? Two tureens may be used for the offering.
en.judgmentNote: Two grain vessels are set at the plain offering after burial (儀禮, 士虞禮); the songs count eight tureens at a feast, and four at a meal in better days (伐木, 權輿). Two is the smallest number the sources show. 享 is the offering, the bronzes' word.
en.tradition: The top line below is reduced to add to the top line above: reducing below to add above, stripping the people to serve the lord. If one reduces what should be reduced, and in good faith, the reading will answer with the four that follow; in a time of reducing the plainest offering does no harm.
en.image: Below the mountain there is the lake: Reduction. So the noble one checks his anger and stops up his desires.
en.imageNote: A later layer, and moral in its own words. 懲 in the songs is to check, to be warned (小毖). Nothing is better reduced than anger and desire (王弼). To check is to stop what has come; to stop up, to close off what is to come (孔穎達).

lines.text: The affair stopped, going quickly: no blame. Ladling, reduce it.
lines.note: 遄, quickly, is the songs' word (相鼠, 崧高). The Chu records pair speed and thanks: if what is wished for is got quickly, give thanks quickly (包山 200). 酌 is ladling wine (行葦); the commentators read it as weighing. 虞翻's text has 祀事, the offering.

lines.text: A favourable divination. Campaigning: disaster. Not reducing: adding to it.
lines.note: The verdicts are the book's fixed words; the sources give nothing for the line's matter. If the second line also reduced itself, the figure would be 剝: so it holds still and adds (王弼).

lines.text: Three people going: then one person is reduced. One person going: then he gets his companion.
lines.note: The 繫辭下, a later wing, reads it with heaven and earth intertwining and man and woman joining: "it speaks of coming to one". In the songs 友 is the friend or mate (關雎). 朱熹: two together are single-minded, three are mixed and in disorder.

lines.text: Reducing its illness: making it quick, there is joy. No blame.
lines.note: The Chu records put illness and delay to the oracle and answer in this line's words: "very auspicious, within the term there will be joy" (包山 198); "if what is wished for is got quickly ..." (包山 200). 喜 is a verdict word there, and 速 stands where this line has 遄.

lines.text: Someone adds to it. A turtle of ten strings of cowries cannot go against it. Greatly auspicious.
lines.note: In the bronzes 朋 is a string of cowries, counted in gifts ("貝十朋", 集成 04030) and as a price (NA1439). The turtle of divination is the treasure of the state (大誥). 違 is to go against, as the turtle's crack goes against or follows a plan (侯果). The phrase stands again in 42 六二.

lines.text: Not reducing: adding to it. No blame. The divination: auspicious. Favourable to have somewhere to go. Getting servants, without households.
lines.note: In the bronzes servants are given by the household: "臣五家", five households of servants (集成 04328); "臣二百家" (集成 06015). 得臣无家 sets the two words of that count side by side. The commentators: all are its servants, and there is no separate house.

essays.title: The lake below the mountain
essays.text: The lower trigram is the lake, the upper the mountain. 鄭玄: the lake lessens itself to add to the mountain's height, as the lords lessen the wealth of their states to bring tribute to the Son of Heaven. 損 and 益 are one figure turned over, and the turtle of ten strings of cowries stands in both. The words of offering run through the hexagram: the offering and two tureens in the judgment, the turtle of the fifth line.

readings.title: Ten strings of cowries?
readings.text: A turtle worth ten strings (崔憬; the bronzes' 朋 as gift and price); ten kinds of turtle (馬融, 鄭玄); ten pairs of turtles (朱熹, Wilhelm, Legge); many helpers (王弼, 程頤). We print the cowries: no other sense makes a phrase. By our cut the turtle "cannot go against it"; for 王弼 and 朱熹 it is a gift to accept.

readings.title: The affair stopped, or the offering?
readings.text: The base has 已事, the affair stopped or finished (孔穎達, 王弼, 程頤, 朱熹). 虞翻's text has 祀事, the offering, which would join the line to the judgment's offering and the turtle. We print the base.

readings.title: Ladling or weighing?
readings.text: The songs' 酌 is ladling wine; every commentator reads weighing, or taking (虞翻). "Ladling" keeps the word; it does not say what is ladled.

readings.title: Servants without households?
readings.text: Servants counted by households, as in the bronzes; or no separate house, all within the realm (王弼, 王肅, 程頤, Legge); or no home of one's own (Wilhelm). We print "without households", which leaves whose open.

pinyinTones.name: Sǔn
pinyinTones.judgment: yǒu fú, yuán jí, wú jiù, kě zhēn. lì yǒu yōu wǎng. hé zhī yòng, èr guǐ kě yòng xiǎng.
pinyinTones.image: shān xià yǒu zé, sǔn. jūn zǐ yǐ chéng fèn zhì yù.
lines: yǐ shì chuán wǎng, wú jiù. zhuó sǔn zhī.
lì zhēn. zhēng xiōng, fú sǔn, yì zhī.
sān rén xíng zé sǔn yī rén, yī rén xíng zé dé qí yǒu.
sǔn qí jí, shǐ chuán yǒu xǐ, wú jiù.
huò yì zhī, shí péng zhī guī fú kè wéi, yuán jí.
fú sǔn, yì zhī, wú jiù, zhēn jí, lì yǒu yōu wǎng, dé chén wú jiā.

pinyinNotes: 損: sǔn, as 陸德明 孫本反
曷: hé, as 陸德明 何葛反
享: xiǎng (to offer), as 陸德明 香兩反
已: yǐ, as 陸德明 音以
遄: chuán, as 陸德明 市專反

hexagrams.image: 風雷，益。君子以見善則遷，有過則改。

lines.label: 初九
lines.text: 利用為大作，元吉，无咎。

lines.label: 六二
lines.text: 或益之，十朋之龜弗克違。永貞吉。王用享于帝，吉。

lines.label: 六三
lines.text: 益之，用凶事无咎。有孚，中行。告公用圭。

lines.label: 六四
lines.text: 中行告公，從，利用為依遷國。

lines.label: 九五
lines.text: 有孚惠心，勿問，元吉。有孚惠我德。

lines.label: 上九
lines.text: 莫益之，或擊之，立心勿恆，凶。

hexagrams.heading: 益
hexagrams.name: 益

wilhelm.name: Die Mehrung
wilhelm.judgment: Die Mehrung. Fördernd ist es, etwas zu unternehmen. Fördernd ist es, das große Wasser zu durchqueren.
wilhelm.image: Wind und Donner: das Bild der Mehrung. So der Edle: Sieht er Gutes, so ahmt er es nach, hat er Fehler, so legt er sie ab.
lines: Anfangs eine Neun bedeutet: Fördernd ist es, große Taten zu vollbringen. Erhabenes Heil! Kein Makel.
Sechs auf zweitem Platz bedeutet: Es mehrt ihn wohl jemand. Zehn Paar Schildkröten können dem nicht widerstreben. Dauernde Beharrlichkeit bringt Heil. Der König stellt ihn dar vor Gott. Heil!
Sechs auf drittem Platz bedeutet: Man wird gemehrt durch unheilvolle Ereignisse. Kein Makel, wenn du wahrhaftig bist und in der Mitte wandelst und dem Fürsten berichtest mit einem Siegel.
Sechs auf viertem Platz bedeutet: Wenn du in der Mitte wandelst und dem Fürsten berichtest, so wird er folgen. Fördernd ist es, benützt zu werden bei der Verlegung der Hauptstadt.
Neun auf fünftem Platz bedeutet: Wenn du wahrhaftig ein gütiges Herz hast, so frage nicht. Erhabenes Heil! Wahrhaftig wird Güte als deine Tugend erkannt werden.
Oben eine Neun bedeutet: Er gereicht niemand zur Mehrung. Es schlägt ihn wohl gar jemand. Er hält sein Herz nicht dauernd fest. Unheil!
wilhelm.source: Richard Wilhelm, I Ging (Jena, 1924), as transcribed with modernised spelling at schuledesrades.org

legge.name: Yî
legge.judgment: Yî indicates that (in the state which it denotes) there will be advantage in every movement which shall be undertaken, that it will be advantageous (even) to cross the great stream.
legge.image: (The trigram representing) wind and that for thunder form Yî. The superior man, in accordance with this, when he sees what is good, moves towards it; and when he sees his errors, he turns from them.
lines: The first line, undivided, shows that it will be advantageous for its subject in his position to make a great movement. If it be greatly fortunate, no blame will be imputed to him.

The second line, divided, shows parties adding to the stores of its subject ten pairs of tortoise shells whose oracles cannot be opposed. Let him persevere in being firm and correct, and there will be good fortune. Let the king, (having the virtues thus distinguished), employ them in presenting his offerings to God, and there will be good fortune.

The third line, divided, shows increase given to its subject by means of what is evil, so that he shall (be led to good), and be without blame. Let him be sincere and pursue the path of the Mean, (so shall he secure the recognition of the ruler, like) an officer who announces himself to his prince by the symbol of his rank.
The fourth line, divided, shows its subject pursuing the due course. His advice to his prince is followed. He can with advantage be relied on in such a movement as that of removing the capital.

The fifth line, undivided, shows its subject with sincere heart seeking to benefit (all below). There need be no question about it; the result will be great good fortune. (All below) will with sincere heart acknowledge his goodness.
In the sixth line, undivided, we see one to whose increase none will contribute, while many will seek to assail him. He observes no regular rule in the ordering of his heart. There will be evil.
legge.source: James Legge, The Yi King (Sacred Books of the East 16, 1882), pp. 149-150 (Image: Appendix II, p. 319)

en.name: Increase
en.nameNote: 益 is to add to, to increase: "增長之名" (陸德明). The 彖: reducing what is above and adding to what is below, the people's joy has no bound. In the lines 益 is "adding to", as in 41.
en.judgment: Favourable to have somewhere to go. Favourable to ford the great river.
en.judgmentNote: The two verdicts are the book's fixed words. 鄭玄 reads the hexagram as a ruler giving to his lords: the Son of Heaven lessens what he has to give to those below, as a lord issues orders and his ministers carry them out.
en.tradition: 益 is increasing: the first line of the upper trigram goes down below the lower; the fifth and second lines are both central and right; thunder and wind are both wood: so the reading is favourable to go, and favourable to ford the great river.
en.image: Wind and thunder: Increase. So the noble one, seeing good, moves to it; having faults, changes them.
en.imageNote: A later layer, and moral in its own words. Nothing adds more than moving to the good and changing faults (王弼). Wind and thunder add to each other, and so do moving to the good and changing faults (朱熹).

lines.text: Favourable to use in doing great works. Greatly auspicious. No blame.
lines.note: The 繫辭下, a later wing, says the plough was taken from this hexagram, and 虞翻 reads 大作 as ploughing and sowing. The king's ploughing of the thousand-mu field, led by the Grand Scribe, is in the 國語. 孔穎達 reads great undertakings, as the building in 緜.

lines.text: Someone adds to it. A turtle of ten strings of cowries cannot go against it. The divination for the long run: auspicious. The king uses it in an offering to the High God: auspicious.
lines.note: 十朋之龜 as 41 六五: the bronzes' count of cowries. The king's offering to the High God is in the songs' prayer for grain (噫嘻) and the bronzes (天亡簋). 朱熹: an auspicious reading for divining about the suburban offering to Heaven.

lines.text: Adding to it: used in affairs of disaster, no blame. There is confirmation, in the middle file. Announcing to the duke, using a jade tablet.
lines.note: 凶事 are mourning, famine and calamity in the rites (周禮, 大宗伯). In the 金縢 the Duke of Zhou holds a jade tablet, announces to the ancestors, and then divines with three turtles. The tablet is the token of rank (韓奕). 中行 is the middle file of a column.

lines.text: In the middle file, announcing to the duke: followed. Favourable to use in being a support for moving the state.
lines.note: When Zhou moved east it leaned on Jin and Zheng (左傳, 隱公六年), cited here by 崔憬, 孔穎達 and 朱熹. Moving a capital was put to the oracle: 盤庚 consults the turtle, and the Zhou cut their turtle before building (緜). 朱熹: an auspicious reading for moving a state.

lines.text: There is trust: a kind heart. Do not ask: greatly auspicious. There is trust: it grants me favour.
lines.note: 惠 with 我 and what is granted is the songs' construction: "惠我無疆", grants us without bound (烈文). 問, to ask, is divination's question: 貞 is "卜問也" (說文). So 勿問: the answer needs no question (程頤).

lines.text: None adds to it; someone strikes it. Setting the heart, not keeping it constant: disaster.
lines.note: The 繫辭下, a later wing: if the nobleman asks without ties, the people will not join him; when none joins him, those who would harm him come. 恆 is constancy, as 32. 勿 is read as the negative of a state, since 凶 follows as the outcome (孔穎達).

essays.title: Wind over thunder
essays.text: The lower trigram is thunder, the upper wind, and wood: the 彖 says the way of wood goes on, for fording the great river. The figure is 41 turned over, and 41's turtle of ten strings of cowries stands here in the second line. The lines name the king's offering to the High God, the duke and the tablet, and the moving of a state.

readings.title: Ploughing, or great works?
readings.text: Ploughing and sowing: 虞翻, 侯果, with the 繫辭下's plough taken from this hexagram. Great undertakings: 孔穎達, 程頤, 朱熹, Wilhelm, Legge. We print "great works", which holds both.

readings.title: Grants me favour?
readings.text: 惠 as the songs' verb with 我 (烈文): "grants me favour". 王弼 and 程頤: "they are kind to my virtue". Wilhelm and Legge: my goodness will be acknowledged. We print "grants me favour".

readings.title: A state, or a warning?
readings.text: 立心勿恆 is a state, "not keeping it constant" (孔穎達, 王弼, Wilhelm, Legge), or a warning, "do not keep it constant" (程頤, 朱熹). We print the state.

readings.title: Ask, or speak?
readings.text: 勿問 is "do not ask", divination's question (程頤: known without asking), or "do not speak of it" (崔憬). We print "do not ask".

pinyinTones.name: Yì
pinyinTones.judgment: lì yǒu yōu wǎng. lì shè dà chuān.
pinyinTones.image: fēng léi, yì. jūn zǐ yǐ jiàn shàn zé qiān, yǒu guò zé gǎi.
lines: lì yòng wéi dà zuò, yuán jí, wú jiù.
huò yì zhī, shí péng zhī guī fú kè wéi. yǒng zhēn jí. wáng yòng xiǎng yú dì, jí.
yì zhī, yòng xiōng shì wú jiù. yǒu fú, zhōng xíng. gào gōng yòng guī.
zhōng xíng gào gōng, cóng, lì yòng wéi yī qiān guó.
yǒu fú huì xīn, wù wèn, yuán jí. yǒu fú huì wǒ dé.
mò yì zhī, huò jī zhī, lì xīn wù héng, xiōng.

pinyinNotes: 益: yì
為: wéi (to do, to make)
享: xiǎng (to offer), as 陸德明 香兩反
中行: zhōng xíng (the middle way)

hexagrams.judgment: 揚于王庭，孚號，有厲。告自邑，不利即戎。利有攸往。
hexagrams.image: 澤上於天，夬。君子以施祿及下，居德則忌。

lines.label: 初九
lines.text: 壯于前趾，往不勝，為咎。

lines.label: 九二
lines.text: 惕號，莫夜有戎，勿恤。

lines.label: 九三
lines.text: 壯于頄，有凶。君子夬夬，獨行遇雨，若濡，有慍，无咎。

lines.label: 九四
lines.text: 臀无膚，其行次且。牽羊，悔亡。聞言不信。

lines.label: 九五
lines.text: 莧陸夬夬，中行无咎。

lines.label: 上六
lines.text: 无號，終有凶。

hexagrams.heading: 夬
hexagrams.name: 夬

wilhelm.name: Der Durchbruch, (die Entschlossenheit)
wilhelm.judgment: Der Durchbruch. Entschlossen muss man am Hof des Königs die Sache bekanntmachen. Der Wahrheit gemäß muss sie verkündet werden. Gefahr! Man muss seine eigene Stadt benachrichtigen. Nicht fördernd ist es, zu den Waffen zu greifen. Fördernd ist es, etwas zu unternehmen.
wilhelm.image: Der See ist an den Himmel emporgestiegen: das Bild des Durchbruchs. So spendet der Edle Reichtum nach unten hin und scheut es, bei seiner Tugend zu verweilen.
lines: Anfangs eine Neun bedeutet: Mächtig in den vorwärtsschreitenden Zehen. Geht man hin und ist der Sache nicht gewachsen, so macht man einen Fehler.
Neun auf zweitem Platz bedeutet: Alarmruf. Abends und nachts Waffen. Fürchte nichts.

Neun auf drittem Platz bedeutet: Mächtig in den Backenknochen zu sein bringt Unheil. Der Edle ist fest entschlossen. Er wandelt einsam und kommt in den Regen. Er wird bespritzt, und man murrt wider ihn. Kein Makel.

Neun auf viertem Platz bedeutet: An den Oberschenkeln ist keine Haut, und das Gehen fällt schwer. Ließe man sich führen wie ein Schaf, so würde die Reue schwinden. Wenn man aber diese Worte hört, so wird man sie nicht glauben.
Neun auf fünftem Platz bedeutet: Dem Unkraut gegenüber braucht es feste Entschlossenheit. In der Mitte wandeln bleibt frei von Makel.
Oben eine Sechs bedeutet: Kein Ruf! Schließlich kommt Unheil.
wilhelm.source: Richard Wilhelm, I Ging (Jena, 1924), as transcribed with modernised spelling at schuledesrades.org

legge.name: Kwâi
legge.judgment: Kwâi requires (in him who would fulfil its meaning) the exhibition (of the culprit’s guilt) in the royal court, and a sincere and earnest appeal (for sympathy and support), with a consciousness of the peril (involved in cutting off the criminal). He should (also) make announcement in his own city, and show that it will not be well to have recourse at once to arms. (In this way) there will be advantage in whatever he shall go forward to.
legge.image: (The trigram representing) heaven and that for the waters of a marsh mounting above it form Kwâi. The superior man, in accordance with this, bestows emolument on those below him, and dislikes allowing his gifts to accumulate (undispensed).
lines: The first line, undivided, shows its subject in (the pride of) strength advancing with his toes. He goes forward, but will not succeed. There will be ground for blame.

The second line, undivided, shows its subject full of apprehension and appealing (for sympathy and help). Late at night hostile measures may be (taken against him), but he need not be anxious about them.

The third line, undivided, shows its subject (about to advance) with strong (and determined) looks. There will be evil. (But) the superior man, bent on cutting off (the criminal), will walk alone and encounter the rain, (till he be hated by his proper associates) as if he were contaminated (by the others). (In the end) there will be no blame against him.

The fourth line, undivided, shows one from whose buttocks the skin has been stripped, and who walks slowly and with difficulty. (If he could act) like a sheep led (after its companions), occasion for repentance would disappear. But though he hear these words, he will not believe them.

The fifth line, undivided, shows (the small men like) a bed of purslain, which ought to be uprooted with the utmost determination. (The subject of the line having such determination), his action, in harmony with his central position, will lead to no error or blame.
The sixth line, divided, shows its subject without any (helpers) on whom to call. His end will be evil.
legge.source: James Legge, The Yi King (Sacred Books of the East 16, 1882), pp. 151-153 (Image: Appendix II, p. 320)

en.name: Breakthrough (Resoluteness)
en.nameNote: 夬 is to part, to cut off, to decide: "決也" (彖, 序卦, 雜卦). The 雜卦: the hard cuts off the soft. The 左傳 names the hexagram in 513 BC. In the lines 夬 stands doubled, "resolute, resolute", keeping 10 九五's 夬履.
en.judgment: Raised up at the king's court. Captives cry out. There is danger. Announcing from the town: not favourable to approach the troops. Favourable to have somewhere to go.
en.judgmentNote: One received by the king stood in the middle of the court and "對揚", extolled, the king's grace (七年趞曹鼎; 江漢). Covenants were sworn and suits pleaded at the king's court (左傳, 632 and 563 BC). 號 is crying out in the songs (碩鼠). 告自邑 as 11 上六.
en.tradition: The yang cut off the yin, the hexagram of the third month. In doing so one must name its crime rightly and with full sincerity call out to the multitude to join their strength; there is still danger; one must first order one's own affairs and not rely on force alone: then it is favourable to go.
en.image: The lake goes up to heaven: Breakthrough. So the noble one bestows emoluments to reach those below; resting on his virtue is then forbidden.
en.imageNote: A later layer, and moral in its own words. 祿 is a word of the bronzes' prayers: "用祈百祿" (集成 02777). The lake above heaven must come down and soak what is below (王弼). 朱熹 says he does not understand 居德則忌.

lines.text: Strength in the forward toes. Going on, not winning: that is blame.
lines.note: 34 初九 壯于趾 with "forward" added, and its own verdict. 勝 is the 左傳's word for winning a fight: "an army prevails by concord, not by numbers" (桓公十一年). The small image turns the words round: "not winning and going on".

lines.text: Alarm, crying out. At evening and night there are troops. Do not be anxious.
lines.note: The 左傳 tells of attacks by night: Zheng fell on the camps of Song, Qi and Wei (575 BC), and the Chu army broke in the night (547 BC). 莫 is read 暮, evening (陸德明). 恤, anxiety, stands beside a divination in 杕杜.

lines.text: Strength in the cheekbones: there is disaster. The nobleman: resolute, resolute. Going alone, he meets rain, as if soaked. There is resentment. No blame.
lines.note: Going alone is the songs' lament: "獨行踽踽" (杕杜); rain falls on the man coming back from campaign (東山). 慍 is resentment, "慍于群小" (柏舟). The Chu slip has 有厲, danger, for 有慍. 頄 is the cheekbone (陸德明).

lines.text: Buttocks without skin; his going falters. Leading a sheep: regret gone. Hearing talk, not believing it.
lines.note: In 597 BC the lord of Zheng, his shoulder bared, led a sheep out to meet the Chu king in surrender (左傳, 宣公十二年). 牽 is to lead on a rope (說文). The Chu slip has 喪羊, losing the sheep. 次且 is stepping back and not going forward (馬融).

lines.text: The pokeweed: resolute, resolute. In the middle file: no blame.
lines.note: The 爾雅 lists both plants the readers name: the red amaranth and 蔏陸, pokeweed. 馬融, 鄭玄 and 王肅 read one plant, 商陸. 王弼: a soft, brittle weed, cut with the utmost ease. 中行 is the middle file of a column.

lines.text: No crying out. In the end there is disaster.
lines.note: The Chu slip has 忘號，中有凶. 王弼: no crying can prolong it. 朱熹: none of its kind left to call to. 程頤 rejects reading 號 here as a command.

essays.title: Five strong lines under one weak
essays.text: The lower trigram is heaven, the upper the lake. Five whole lines stand under one broken one, the last of the six figures in which the whole lines grow; 朱熹 calls it the hexagram of the third month. The readers take the top line for a small man in a high place, to be cut away by the five. The next hexagram, 姤, is this one turned over, and repeats this fourth line's buttocks without skin word for word.

readings.title: Raised up at the king's court?
readings.text: Made public at the court (王弼, 孔穎達, 程頤, 朱熹); passing over, the yin line over the yang (鄭玄); the bronzes' 對揚, the response of one received at court, which no reader says. Wilhelm and Legge supply a culprit. We print "raised up", which supplies none.

readings.title: Captives cry out?
readings.text: The commentators read 孚 as good faith and 號 as a command (王弼, 程頤), or a call to the multitude (朱熹). Shaughnessy reads captives crying out, as the bronzes' 俘. We print "captives cry out", as this edition renders 孚 by its context.

readings.title: The order of the third line
readings.text: 程頤 calls the line disordered: 胡瑗 moved "resolute, resolute" after the resentment, and 程頤 would put it after the rain. 王弼, 孔穎達, 朱熹 and the Chu slip have the base's order. We print it.

readings.title: Which plant?
readings.text: One plant, pokeweed (馬融, 鄭玄, 王肅, 王弼); amaranth and pokeweed (董遇, 宋衷); the purslane (程頤, 朱熹, Legge); smiling and concord (虞翻). We print "the pokeweed".

readings.title: Leading or losing the sheep?
readings.text: The base and every reader: leading a sheep, and the 左傳's surrender shows the act in its time. The Chu slip: losing the sheep, as 34 六五. We print the base.

pinyinTones.name: Guài
pinyinTones.judgment: yáng yú wáng tíng, fú háo, yǒu lì. gào zì yì, bù lì jí róng. lì yǒu yōu wǎng.
pinyinTones.image: zé shàng yú tiān, guài. jūn zǐ yǐ shì lù jí xià, jū dé zé jì.
lines: zhuàng yú qián zhǐ, wǎng bù shèng, wéi jiù.
tì háo, mù yè yǒu róng, wù xù.
zhuàng yú kuí, yǒu xiōng. jūn zǐ guài guài, dú xíng yù yǔ, ruò rú, yǒu yùn, wú jiù.
tún wú fū, qí xíng cī qū. qiān yáng, huǐ wáng. wén yán bù xìn.
xiàn lù guài guài, zhōng xíng wú jiù.
wú háo, zhōng yǒu xiōng.

pinyinNotes: 夬: guài, as 陸德明 古快反
施: shì (to bestow), as 陸德明 始豉反
號: háo (to cry out), as 陸德明 户羔反, against 鄭玄 and 王廙's hào
莫 (莫夜): mù (evening, read 暮), as 陸德明 音暮
頄: kuí (the cheekbone), as 陸德明 求龜反
慍: yùn, as 陸德明 紆運反
臀: tún, as 陸德明 徒敦反
次且: cī qū (halting, 趑趄), as 陸德明 七私反 and 七餘反; modern zī jū
莧: xiàn, as 陸德明 閑辯反

hexagrams.image: 天下有風，姤。后以施命誥四方。

lines.label: 初六
lines.text: 繫于金柅，貞吉。有攸往，見凶。羸豕孚，蹢躅。

lines.label: 九二
lines.text: 包有魚，无咎，不利賓。

lines.label: 九三
lines.text: 臀无膚，其行次且，厲，无大咎。

lines.label: 九四
lines.text: 包无魚，起凶。

lines.label: 九五
lines.text: 以杞包瓜，含章，有隕自天。

lines.label: 上九
lines.text: 姤其角，吝，无咎。

hexagrams.heading: 姤
hexagrams.name: 姤

wilhelm.name: Das Entgegenkommen
wilhelm.judgment: Das Entgegenkommen. Das Mädchen ist mächtig. Man soll ein solches Mädchen nicht heiraten.
wilhelm.image: Unter dem Himmel ist der Wind: das Bild des Entgegenkommens. So macht es der Fürst beim Verbreiten seiner Befehle und ihrer Verkündigung an die vier Himmelsgegenden.
lines: Anfangs eine Sechs bedeutet: Man muss es hemmen mit ehernem Radschuh. Beharrlichkeit ist von Heil. Wenn man es hingehen lässt, so erfährt man Unheil. Auch ein mageres Schwein hat die Anlage dazu, umherzutoben.
Neun auf zweitem Platz bedeutet: Im Behälter ist ein Fisch. Kein Makel! Nicht fördernd für Gäste.
Neun auf drittem Platz bedeutet: An den Oberschenkeln ist keine Haut, und das Gehen fällt schwer. Wenn man der Gefahr eingedenk ist, macht man keinen großen Fehler.
Neun auf viertem Platz bedeutet: Im Behälter ist kein Fisch. Daraus erhebt sich Unheil.
Neun auf fünftem Platz bedeutet: Mit Weidenblättern bedeckte Melone: verborgene Linien. Da fällt es einem vom Himmel herunter zu.
Oben eine Neun bedeutet: Er kommt mit seinen Hörnern entgegen. Beschämung. Kein Makel.
wilhelm.source: Richard Wilhelm, I Ging (Jena, 1924), as transcribed with modernised spelling at schuledesrades.org

legge.name: Kâu
legge.judgment: Kâu shows a female who is bold and strong. It will not be good to marry (such) a female.
legge.image: (The trigram representing) wind and that for the sky above it form Kâu. The sovereign, in accordance with this, delivers his charges, and promulgates his announcements throughout the four quarters (of the kingdom).
lines: The first line, divided, shows how its subject should be kept (like a carriage) tied and fastened to a metal drag, in which case with firm correctness there will be good fortune. (But) if he move in any direction, evil will appear. He will be (like) a lean pig, which is sure to keep jumping about.
The second line, undivided, shows its subject with a wallet of fish. There will be no error. But it will not be well to let (the subject of the first line) go forward to the guests.
The third line, undivided, shows one from whose buttocks the skin has been stripped so that he walks with difficulty. The position is perilous, but there will be no great error.
The fourth line, undivided, shows its subject with his wallet, but no fish in it. This will give rise to evil.
The fifth line, undivided, (shows its subject as) a medlar tree overspreading the gourd (beneath it). If he keep his brilliant qualities concealed, (a good issue) will descend (as) from Heaven.
The sixth line, undivided, shows its subject receiving others on his horns. There will be occasion for regret, but there will be no error.
legge.source: James Legge, The Yi King (Sacred Books of the East 16, 1882), pp. 154-155 (Image: Appendix II, p. 321)

en.name: Coming to Meet
en.nameNote: 姤 is to meet: "遇也" (彖, 序卦, 雜卦). The old text and 鄭玄 write 遘, "遇也" (爾雅, 說文). 朱熹: it comes upon one suddenly, unlooked for, like a meeting not arranged. In the top line it is the verb, "meeting its horns".
en.judgment: The woman is strong. Not to be used for taking a wife.
en.judgmentNote: Marriages were put to the stalks and refused: Duke Xian of Jin's for his daughter (左傳, 645 BC), and 崔杼's in 548 BC, where the wind trigram "brings down the wife: she may not be married". He married her, and it ended in ruin. 勿用取女 as 4 六三.
en.tradition: When the cutting off is complete the figure is pure Heaven, the fourth month; with 姤 a yin line is seen again, the fifth month. A meeting is already not right, and one yin meeting five yang is a woman's virtue unfaithful and strong in the extreme; to take her as a mate must harm the yang.
en.image: Below heaven there is the wind: Coming to Meet. So the sovereign issues commands and proclaims them to the four quarters.
en.imageNote: A later layer, and moral in its own words. 誥 is the word of the early Zhou proclamations: "大誥爾多邦" (大誥). The four quarters are the bronzes' and the songs' world. As grass bends before the wind, the ruler sends out his commands (孔穎達).

lines.text: Tied to a bronze brake. The divination: auspicious. Having somewhere to go: disaster is seen. A pig tangled: a captive; pacing and stamping.
lines.note: At a wedding a pig and fourteen fish fill the cauldrons (儀禮, 士昏禮); the line names no wedding. In a song pigs with white hooves wading are a sign of rain (漸漸之石). 柅 is a brake (馬融) or a reel (說文, 王肅). 羸 is the rope that ties a pig (宋衷).

lines.text: The wrapping has fish. No blame. Not favourable for guests.
lines.note: Fish and taking a wife stand in one couplet: "豈其食魚 ... 豈其取妻" (衡門). Fish were supplied for offerings and guests (周禮). 包 is wrapping, as the dead deer "白茅包之" (野有死麕); 孔穎達 reads the kitchen, the Chu slip a sack.

lines.text: Buttocks without skin; his going falters. Danger. No great blame.
lines.note: The first two phrases are 43 九四's, and the same in the Chu slip. 无大咎 is the verdict of 18 九三. In its proper place, the danger is not of its own making (王弼).

lines.text: The wrapping without fish. Rising: disaster.
lines.note: The Chu slip: 橐亡魚，已(起)凶. 起 in the songs is to rise and go: "載起載行" (沔水); the august Corpse rises (楚茨). 程頤 reads "disaster arises": the people gone, trouble is coming.

lines.text: With osier, wrapping a melon. Holding its pattern within. There is a falling from heaven.
lines.note: 杞 in the songs is a shrub of the hills, the wolfberry (四牡, 毛傳); 鄭玄 reads the osier. Melons were eaten in the seventh month and offered to the ancestors (七月, 信南山). 含章 is 2 六三's phrase. 朱熹: what was not, suddenly there.

lines.text: Meeting its horns. Trouble. No blame.
lines.note: Horns in the book: 34 九三, 35 上九. The Chu slip writes the line with the hexagram's name 敂. 王弼: at the end there is nothing more to meet but the horns; it does not fight, so no disaster.

essays.title: One soft line under five strong
essays.text: The lower trigram is wind, the upper heaven: "below heaven there is the wind". The figure is 43 turned over, one broken line under five whole ones; 朱熹 makes it the hexagram of the fifth month. The readers take the bottom line for a woman meeting five men. The lines name things tied, wrapped and carried: a bronze brake or reel, a pig, fish in a wrapping, a melon wrapped in osier.

readings.title: A brake, and a lean or tangled pig?
readings.text: 柅 is a brake under a cart (馬融, 程頤, 朱熹, Wilhelm, Legge) or a reeling tool (王肅, the 說文). 羸 is roped (宋衷, 陸績, as 34) or lean (王弼, 程頤, Wilhelm, Legge). We print "a brake" and "tangled", which keeps 34's word and the line's tying; 孚 is "a captive" by context.

readings.title: A wrapping, a kitchen, a sack?
readings.text: To wrap (虞翻, 程頤); the kitchen, 庖 (copies in 陸德明; 王弼, 孔穎達); the Chu slip's sack. We print "the wrapping".

readings.title: Which 杞?
readings.text: The osier (鄭玄, 薛虞, Wilhelm); the wolfberry (毛傳 on the songs; 王弼); a great tree (馬融, 程頤, 朱熹); the medlar (Legge). We print "osier", the tree that can be bent to wrap; the songs' wolfberry is the strongest case against it.

readings.title: Falling from heaven?
readings.text: A gift come down from heaven (程頤, 朱熹, Wilhelm), or it can be brought down only by heaven (王弼, 孔穎達). We print "there is a falling from heaven", which keeps both open.

pinyinTones.name: Gòu
pinyinTones.judgment: nǚ zhuàng, wù yòng qǔ nǚ.
pinyinTones.image: tiān xià yǒu fēng, gòu. hòu yǐ shì mìng gào sì fāng.
lines: xì yú jīn nǐ, zhēn jí. yǒu yōu wǎng, jiàn xiōng. léi shǐ fú, zhí zhú.
bāo yǒu yú, wú jiù, bù lì bīn.
tún wú fū, qí xíng cī qū, lì, wú dà jiù.
bāo wú yú, qǐ xiōng.
yǐ qǐ bāo guā, hán zhāng, yǒu yǔn zì tiān.
gòu qí jiǎo, lìn, wú jiù.

pinyinNotes: 姤: gòu (to meet), as 陸德明 古豆反
取: qǔ (to take a wife, read 娶), as 陸德明 用娶 七喻反
施: shì (to bestow), as 陸德明 始豉反 (43, 42's 彖)
誥: gào, as 陸德明 古報反
柅: nǐ, as 徐邈 乃履反 in 陸德明
羸: léi, as 陸德明 劣隨反
蹢躅: zhí zhú, as 陸德明 直㦸反 and 直録反
包: bāo (wrapping), the book's sense; 陸德明 reads 庖, 白交反 (páo)
臀: tún
次且: cī qū (halting, 趑趄), as 陸德明 at 43; modern zī jū
杞: qǐ, as 陸德明 音起

hexagrams.judgment: 亨。王假有廟。利見大人。亨。利貞。用大牲，吉。利有攸往。
hexagrams.image: 澤上於地，萃。君子以除戎器，戒不虞。

lines.label: 初六
lines.text: 有孚不終，乃亂乃萃，若號，一握為笑，勿恤，往无咎。

lines.label: 六二
lines.text: 引吉，无咎，孚乃利用禴。

lines.label: 六三
lines.text: 萃如嗟如，无攸利，往无咎，小吝。

lines.label: 九四
lines.text: 大吉，无咎。

lines.label: 九五
lines.text: 萃有位，无咎。匪孚，元，永貞悔亡。

lines.label: 上六
lines.text: 齎咨涕洟，无咎。

hexagrams.heading: 萃
hexagrams.name: 萃

wilhelm.name: Die Sammlung
wilhelm.judgment: Die Sammlung. Gelingen. Der König naht sich seinem Tempel. Fördernd ist es, den großen Mann zu sehen. Das bringt Gelingen. Fördernd ist Beharrlichkeit. Große Opfer zu bringen schafft Heil. Fördernd ist es, etwas zu unternehmen.
wilhelm.image: Der See ist oberhalb der Erde: das Bild der Sammlung. So erneuert der Edle seine Waffen, um Unvorhergesehenem zu begegnen.
lines: Anfangs eine Sechs bedeutet: Wenn du wahrhaftig bist, doch nicht bis zum Ende, so gibt es bald Verwirrung, bald Sammlung. Wenn du rufst, so kannst du nach einem Griff wieder lachen. Bedauere nicht. Hingehen ist ohne Makel.
Sechs auf zweitem Platz bedeutet: Sich ziehen lassen bringt Heil und bleibt ohne Makel. Wenn man wahrhaftig ist, so ist es auch fördernd, ein kleines Opfer zu bringen.
Sechs auf drittem Platz bedeutet: Sammlung unter Seufzen. Nichts, das fördernd wäre. Hingehen ist ohne Makel. Kleine Beschämung.
Neun auf viertem Platz bedeutet: Großes Heil! Kein Makel.

Neun auf fünftem Platz bedeutet: Wenn man beim Sammeln die nötige Stellung hat, so gibt es keinen Makel. Wenn manche noch nicht wahrhaft dabei sind, so bedarf es erhabener, dauernder Beharrlichkeit, dann schwindet die Reue.
Oben eine Sechs bedeutet: Klagen und Seufzen, Tränen in Strömen! Kein Makel.
wilhelm.source: Richard Wilhelm, I Ging (Jena, 1924), as transcribed with modernised spelling at schuledesrades.org

legge.name: Ȝhui
legge.judgment: In (the state denoted by) Ȝhui, the king will repair to his ancestral temple. It will be advantageous (also) to meet with the great man; and then there will be progress and success, though the advantage must come through firm correctness. The use of great victims will conduce to good fortune; and in whatever direction movement is made, it will be advantageous.
legge.image: (The trigram representing the) earth and that for the waters of a marsh raised above it form Ȝhui. The superior man, in accordance with this, has his weapons of war put in good repair, to be prepared against unforeseen contingencies.
lines: The first line, divided, shows its subject with a sincere desire (for union), but unable to carry it out, so that disorder is brought into the sphere of his union. If he cry out (for help to his proper correlate), all at once (his tears) will give place to smiles. He need not mind (the temporary difficulty); as he goes forward, there will be no error.

The second line, divided, shows its subject led forward (by his correlate). There will be good fortune, and freedom from error. There is entire sincerity, and in that case (even the small offerings of) the vernal sacrifice are acceptable.

The third line, divided, shows its subject striving after union and seeming to sigh, yet nowhere finding any advantage. If he go forward, he will not err, though there may be some small cause for regret.
The fourth line, undivided, shows its subject in such a state that, if he be greatly fortunate, he will receive no blame.

The fifth line, undivided, shows the union (of all) under its subject in the place of dignity. There will be no error. If any do not have confidence in him, let him see to it that (his virtue) be great, long-continued, and firmly correct, and all occasion for repentance will disappear.
The topmost line, divided, shows its subject sighing and weeping; but there will be no error.
legge.source: James Legge, The Yi King (Sacred Books of the East 16, 1882), pp. 156-158 (Image: Appendix II, p. 323)

en.name: The Gathering
en.nameNote: 萃 is to gather, to collect: "聚也" (彖, 序卦). The 序卦: things meet and then gather. The 說文 reads 悴, anxiety, "like the 萃 hexagram of the Changes". The Mawangdui and Qin texts write 卒. In the lines 萃 is "gathering".
en.judgment: An offering. The king comes to the temple. Favourable to see the great man. An offering. A favourable divination. Using a great victim: auspicious. Favourable to have somewhere to go.
en.judgmentNote: In the bronzes the king comes into the temple at dawn and takes his place (大克鼎), and after a victory to the Zhou temple for a feast (虢季子白盤). 假 is that 格. "Small affairs did not use a great victim" (左傳, 641 BC); 鄭玄: the great victim is an ox. A song joins offering and divination (天保).
en.tradition: The lake above the earth, the myriad things gathered; the first 亨 is an intrusion. The king may come into the temple: an auspicious reading for a king divining about an offering. Once gathered, one must see the great man to have success, and it must be right; a great victim can only be had when things are gathered.
en.image: The lake goes up onto the earth: The Gathering. So the noble one puts the gear of war in order and guards against the unforeseen.
en.imageNote: A later layer; its words are a song's: "keep your chariots and horses in order, your bows, arrows and weapons ... to guard against the unforeseen" (抑), quoted in the 左傳 (551 BC). 除 is to put in order (王肅, 陸績); 鄭玄 reads "to put away".

lines.text: There is trust, not to the end: now disorder, now gathering. As if crying out: one grasp, and it turns to laughter. Do not be anxious. Going on: no blame.
lines.note: Weeping, then laughter and a divination stand in one stanza of the songs: "泣涕漣漣 ... 載笑載言。爾卜爾筮" (氓). The Chu slip writes 一握于笑. 王弼 reads 一握 as smallness; 程頤 as "one lump", the whole crowd laughing at it.

lines.text: Drawn: auspicious. No blame. Confirmation: then favourable to use in the yue offering.
lines.note: 禴 is a seasonal offering to the ancestors in the songs (天保), set in spring or summer by later lists (周禮, 爾雅, 王制). 既濟 九五 sets it against the slaughter of an ox. The 爾雅 counts 引 among the words for "long"; Shaughnessy reads 引吉 as a verdict.

lines.text: Gathering, sighing. Nothing is favourable. Going on: no blame. A little trouble.
lines.note: The verdicts are the book's. 嗟, sighing, is the sigh of 30 九三 and 六五. 王弼: gathering wrongly breeds trouble; better to go to the top line, of the same mind.

lines.text: Very auspicious. No blame.
lines.note: 大吉 is a Shang verdict and the Chu almanac's, as 37 六四. 王弼 and 朱熹 make it a condition: only if very auspicious is there no blame; the Chinese gives two verdicts.

lines.text: Gathering has places. No blame. Not confirmation. Great. The divination for the long run: regret gone.
lines.note: 位 is the place taken at a rite: the king came into the temple and "即位" (大克鼎). 元 and 永貞 are the words of 8's judgment. Shaughnessy thinks the line corrupt to some extent. The readers make 匪孚 "not trusted".

lines.text: Sighing, lamenting; tears from the eyes and the nose. No blame.
lines.note: Tears and snivel stream down in the songs (澤陂). 鄭玄: from the eyes 涕, from the nose 洟. 馬融: 齎咨 is the voice of grief. 虞翻 reads 齎資, gifts for the dead, as the funeral gifts of the 左傳 (720 BC).

essays.title: The lake above the earth
essays.text: The lower trigram is earth, the upper the lake. 程頤: it says the lake goes up onto the earth, water in the act of gathering. The judgment is the book's fullest account of a rite: the king comes to the temple, there is an offering and a great victim, and the second line names a seasonal offering. 59 has the king coming to the temple too. Sighing and weeping close the hexagram.

readings.title: The first offering
readings.text: The first 亨 is in the base, 王肅's text, 王弼 and 孔穎達; absent from the texts of 馬融, 鄭玄, 陸績 and 虞翻 and from the Chu slip; an intrusion to 程頤 and 朱熹. We print the base.

readings.title: One grasp?
readings.text: Small and weak (王弼, 孔穎達); the whole crowd laughing (程頤, 朱熹); a grasp of the hand (虞翻, Wilhelm); 鄭玄's 屋, three households. Legge: "all at once (his tears) will give place to smiles". We print "one grasp", the word.

readings.title: Drawn, or extended?
readings.text: 引 is drawn, led, an act and its verdict (王弼, 虞翻, 程頤, 朱熹, Wilhelm, Legge), or 引吉 is "extended auspiciousness", 引 as long (爾雅; Shaughnessy). We print "drawn".

readings.title: Great alone, or great and long?
readings.text: The base sets 元 off; 虞翻 and 程頤 read 元永貞 together, as do Wilhelm and Legge. We print 元 alone, "great", then "the divination for the long run".

readings.title: Sighs, or funeral gifts?
readings.text: A sigh and lament (王弼, 鄭玄, 馬融, 程頤; the base); gifts for the dead (虞翻, 李鼎祚's text). We print the base.

pinyinTones.name: Cuì
pinyinTones.judgment: hēng. wáng gé yǒu miào. lì jiàn dà rén. hēng. lì zhēn. yòng dà shēng, jí. lì yǒu yōu wǎng.
pinyinTones.image: zé shàng yú dì, cuì. jūn zǐ yǐ chú róng qì, jiè bù yú.
lines: yǒu fú bù zhōng, nǎi luàn nǎi cuì, ruò háo, yī wò wéi xiào, wù xù, wǎng wú jiù.
yǐn jí, wú jiù, fú nǎi lì yòng yuè.
cuì rú jiē rú, wú yōu lì, wǎng wú jiù, xiǎo lìn.
dà jí, wú jiù.
cuì yǒu wèi, wú jiù. fěi fú, yuán, yǒng zhēn huǐ wáng.
jī zī tì tì, wú jiù.

pinyinNotes: 萃: cuì (gathering)
假: gé (to come to, 至也), as 陸德明 更白反, not jiǎ
