hexagrams.judgment: 亨。小狐汔濟，濡其尾，无攸利。
hexagrams.image: 火在水上，未濟。君子以慎辨物居方。

lines.label: 初六
lines.text: 濡其尾，吝。

lines.label: 九二
lines.text: 曳其輪，貞吉。

lines.label: 六三
lines.text: 未濟，征凶。利涉大川。

lines.label: 九四
lines.text: 貞吉，悔亡，震用伐鬼方，三年，有賞于大國。

lines.label: 六五
lines.text: 貞吉，无悔。君子之光，有孚，吉。

lines.label: 上九
lines.text: 有孚于飲酒，无咎。濡其首，有孚失是。

hexagrams.heading: 未濟
hexagrams.name: 未濟

wilhelm.name: Vor der Vollendung
wilhelm.judgment: Vor der Vollendung. Gelingen. Wenn aber der kleine Fuchs, wenn er beinahe den Übergang vollendet hat, mit dem Schwanz ins Wasser kommt, dann ist nichts, das fördernd wäre.
wilhelm.image: Das Feuer ist oberhalb des Wassers: das Bild des Zustands vor dem Übergang. So ist der Edle vorsichtig in der Unterscheidung der Dinge, damit jedes auf seinen Platz kommt.
lines: Anfangs eine Sechs bedeutet: Er kommt mit dem Schwanz ins Wasser. Beschämend.
Neun auf zweitem Platz bedeutet: Er hemmt seine Räder. Beharrlichkeit bringt Heil.
Sechs auf drittem Platz bedeutet: Vor der Vollendung bringt Angriff Unheil. Fördernd ist es, das große Wasser zu durchqueren.
Neun auf viertem Platz bedeutet: Beharrlichkeit bringt Heil. Reue schwindet. Erschütterung, um das Teufelsland zu züchtigen. Drei Jahre lang gibt es Belohnung mit großen Reichen.
Sechs auf fünftem Platz bedeutet: Beharrlichkeit bringt Heil. Keine Reue. Das Licht des Edlen ist wahrhaftig. Heil!
Oben eine Neun bedeutet: In wahrem Vertrauen trinkt man Wein. Kein Makel. Wenn man aber sein Haupt naß macht, so verliert man das in Wahrheit.
wilhelm.source: Richard Wilhelm, I Ging (Jena, 1924), as transcribed with modernised spelling at schuledesrades.org

legge.name: Wei Ȝî
legge.judgment: Wei Ȝî intimates progress and success (in the circumstances which it implies). (We see) a young fox that has nearly crossed (the stream), when its tail gets immersed. There will be no advantage in any way.
legge.image: (The trigram representing) water and that for fire above it form Wei Ȝî. The superior man, in accordance with this, carefully discriminates among (the qualities of) things, and the (different) positions they (naturally) occupy.
lines: The first line, divided, shows its subject (like a fox) whose tail gets immersed. There will be occasion for regret.
The second line, undivided, shows its subject dragging back his (carriage-)wheel. With firmness and correctness there will be good fortune.
The third line, divided, shows its subject, with (the state of things) not yet remedied, advancing on; which will lead to evil. But there will be advantage in (trying to) cross the great stream.

The fourth line, undivided, shows its subject by firm correctness obtaining good fortune, so that all occasion for repentance disappears. Let him stir himself up, as if he were invading the Demon region, where for three years rewards will come to him (and his troops) from the great kingdom.

The fifth line, divided, shows its subject by firm correctness obtaining good fortune, and having no occasion for repentance. (We see in him) the brightness of a superior man, and the possession of sincerity. There will be good fortune.

The topmost line, undivided, shows its subject full of confidence and therefore feasting (quietly). There will be no error. (If he) cherish this confidence, till he (is like the fox who) gets his head immersed, it will fail of what is right.
legge.source: James Legge, The Yi King (Sacred Books of the East 16, 1882), pp. 207-210 (Image: Appendix II, p. 346)

en.name: Before Completion
en.nameNote: 未濟 is 未, not yet, and 濟, to cross: not yet across. The 序卦: things cannot be brought to an end, "故受之以《未濟》，終焉", and the book ends there. The 雜卦: "《未濟》、男之窮也". The name stands in 六三.
en.judgment: An offering. A little fox, almost across, wets its tail. Nothing is favourable.
en.judgmentNote: A song has a fox at the ford of the Qi (有狐, Mao 63). Foxes were taken in Shang hunts (合集 37473) and for furs (七月, Mao 154). 汔 is "almost": "汔可小康" (民勞, Mao 253, 鄭箋 "幾也"); the 說文 has "水涸也", the water dried up. The Chu slip's judgment is lost.
en.tradition: The time before the affair is done: water and fire do not meet, each of no use to the other; every line is out of its place: so, not yet across. 汔 is "almost"; almost across and the tail wet is still not across: what is favourable for one who gets this?
en.image: Fire is above water: Before Completion. So the noble one is careful to tell things apart and to settle each in its quarter.
en.imageNote: A later layer; 辨物 is 13's Image's word. 侯果: fire flames up and water soaks down; in one body their work does not meet. 王弼: "令物各當其所也", each thing in its place. 程頤: fire above water is out of place, so the noble one sets each in its quarter.

lines.text: Wetting its tail. Trouble.
lines.note: 63 初九 has 濡其尾 with "no blame"; here the same words with "trouble". The Chu slip keeps only the verdict, written 閵. 王弼: at the bottom of the peril it cannot cross, but being low and weak it turns back when hemmed in, so trouble, not disaster. 程頤: a beast fording holds up its tail.

lines.text: Dragging its wheels. The divination: auspicious.
lines.note: 63 初九 has 曳其輪. The Chu slip adds 利涉大川 after the verdict. Shaughnessy takes the phrase as the first of an oracle whose rhyming couplet is lost. 程頤: dragging the wheels back slows the advance, a warning against using strength too far. Whether it holds back or is held is left open.

lines.text: Not yet across: campaigning, disaster. Favourable to ford the great river.
lines.note: The Chu slip has the same words, "未凄，征凶，利涉大川": the clash between the two verdicts stood in the text by about 300 BC. 朱熹: going by water, not by land; some suspect a 不 lost before 利. 荀爽 reads a marriage not yet made.

lines.text: The divination: auspicious. Regret gone. Zhen uses it to attack the Gui lands. Three years: there is an award from the great state.
lines.note: An early Western Zhou bronze has the king order a war on the 鬼方, the spoils counted in the temple, a divination, and an award, 賞, of bow, arrows and armour (集成 02839). The early documents call Shang "大國殷" (召誥). The book always puts a person before 用, and 63 九三 has Gaozong there.

lines.text: The divination: auspicious. No regret. The nobleman's light: there is confirmation. Auspicious.
lines.note: 光 is light, glory, as 20 六四's 觀國之光. The shelf gives nothing else particular to the line. 王弼: giving the work to the able and not doing it oneself is the light of the noble; trusting them without doubt, they give their all. 干寶 reads the Duke of Zhou as regent.

lines.text: There is confirmation in drinking wine. No blame. Wetting its head: there is confirmation, losing this.
lines.note: Drinking and blame stand together in the songs: "或湛樂飲酒，或慘慘畏咎" (北山, Mao 205). The early Zhou forbade crowds drinking but at offerings (酒誥). 虞翻: like Zhou Xin of Shang, sunk in wine; 是 is "the right". 王弼: delight carried too far loses its measure.

essays.title: The little fox and the crossing
essays.text: The pair of 63: the same tail, wheels and head, and the same war against the Gui lands. Here the creature is named, a little fox, almost across. The lines run from the tail wetted to the head wetted over wine. The book ends not across: "things cannot be brought to an end" (序卦). Wilhelm: like spring coming out of winter's standstill, "with this hopeful prospect the Book of Changes closes".

readings.title: Almost, or the water dried up?
readings.text: Almost (鄭玄, 虞翻, 朱熹; Wilhelm, Legge); the water dried up, so the fox must wait (說文; 王弼, 干寶, 孔穎達); bold (程頤's 仡). We print "almost".

readings.title: Zhen: a name or a shaking?
readings.text: By the book's construction a person stands before 用, and 63 has Gaozong there, so we print the name Zhen (Shaughnessy). The commentators read shaking with awe (王弼, 孔穎達); Wilhelm "Erschütterung", Legge "stir himself up". No person of the name is found on the shelf.

readings.title: Favourable to ford, or not?
readings.text: Every text, the Chu slip included, has 利涉大川 after 征凶. 朱熹 and Legge's "many critics" suspect a lost 不. We print the base.

readings.title: Losing this, or losing the right?
readings.text: The words say "losing this" (Shaughnessy too); 虞翻 reads 是 as 正, "what is right", 程頤 "失其宜". We print "losing this".

readings.title: From the great state, or a great state?
readings.text: An award from the great state (Legge, Shaughnessy), or the reward of a great state (孔穎達, 王弼; Wilhelm). We print "from", and leave whether Shang or Zhou is meant.

pinyinTones.name: Wèi Jì
pinyinTones.judgment: hēng. xiǎo hú qì jì, rú qí wěi, wú yōu lì.
pinyinTones.image: huǒ zài shuǐ shàng, wèi jì. jūn zǐ yǐ shèn biàn wù jū fāng.

yè qí lún, zhēn jí.
wèi jì, zhēng xiōng. lì shè dà chuān.

汔: qì (almost), 陸德明 許訖反
